content.title: EGOT Winners: All 21 Stars Who've Reached EGOT Status
content.text: Awards Season may be over, but that doesn't mean we can't keep it going in our hearts! ABC Now that we've had a little room to breathe since the 2025 Oscars, I thought it would be fun to look back at past award winners. More specifically, the greatest of the greats. Every award winner is impressive, but EGOT winners (those who have won an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, AND Tony) are operating on a level that most of us can only dream about, so I wanna live vicariously through their accomplishments by looking back at who has EGOT-ed and what projects lead to their god-tier status. 1. Jennifer Hudson Jeff Kravitz / FilmMagic Singer. Actress. Talk show host. Jennifer Hudson can literally do it all. Even since her American Idol days, it was obvious that this powerhouse performer was destined for superstardom, blowing up the music charts with hits like "Spotlight" and "If This Isn't Love" and wowing us all in movies like Dreamgirls and Cats (ok, a little bit LOL on this one, but we do love it, J. Hud!).Emmy: Outstanding Interactive Media for a Daytime Program – Baba Yaga (2021)Grammy: Best R&B Album – Jennifer Hudson (2009)Oscar: Best Actress in a Supporting Role – Dreamgirls (2007)Tony: Best Musical – A Strange Loop (2022) 2. Robert Lopez Alberto E. Rodriguez / Getty Images Bobby Lopez is the man responsible for "Let It Go," "Agatha All Along," and the all songs from The Book of Mormon. So many big pieces of musical culture trace back to Robert, and his EGOT status is a historic one for many reasons. Firstly, he is the youngest person to EGOT, achieving the milestone at just 39 years old. Secondly, he is the first Filipino person to wrangle all four awards. Thirdly, he is the only person to have multiple of each Big Four awards, so he's like an EGOTEGOTEGOT. He's one of the best to ever do it.Emmy: Outstanding Music Direction and Composition – Wonder Pets! (2008)Grammy: Best Musical Theater Album – The Book of Mormon: Original Broadway Cast Recording (2012)Oscar: Best Original Song – "Let It Go" (2014)Tony: Best Original Score – Avenue Q (2004) 3. Audrey Hepburn Bettmann / Bettmann Archive The Breakfast at Tiffany's icon had a nearly 50-year career as an actor, racking up one of the most impressive film and television resumes in history. Sadly, Hepburn never got to enjoy her EGOT status, as she won her final award in 1994 after her death. Emmy: Outstanding Individual Achievement – Informational Programming – Gardens of the World with Audrey Hepburn (1993)Grammy: Best Spoken Word Album for Children – Audrey Hepburn's Enchanted Tales (1994)Oscar: Best Actress in a Leading Role – Roman Holiday (1954)Tony: Distinguished Dramatic Actress – Ondine (1954) 4. Alan Menken Gary Gershoff / Getty Images There is no Disney without Alan Menken. Sorry! Menken's musical contributions to The Little Mermaid, Beauty and the Beast, and Pocahontas made those films what they are. The fact that he has EGOT-ed is maybe the least surprising thing you'll hear all day because the TALENT of this man is coo-coo.Emmy: Outstanding Original Song in a Children's, Young Adult or Animated Program – "Waiting in the Wings" (2020)Grammy: Song of the Year – "A Whole New World (Aladdin's Theme)" (1994)Oscar: Best Original Score – The Little Mermaid (1990)Tony: Best Original Score – Newsies (2012) 5. Rita Moreno Bettmann / Bettmann Archive Rita Moreno is a gotdamn living legend! Known for her role as Anita in West Side Story, the Puerto Rican triple-threat has been in the biz for EIGHTY YEARS! From voicing Carmen in Where on Earth is Carmen Sandiego (!!!!) to her role in the reboot of One Day at a Time, Rita has always stayed in the mix. And that's on staying relevant, hunny! Rita Moreno, you will always be famous. Emmy: Outstanding Continuing or Single Performance by a Supporting Actress in Variety or Music – The Muppet Show (1977)Grammy: Best Recording for Children – The Electric Company (1973)Oscar: Best Actress in a Supporting Role – West Side Story (1962)Tony: Best Supporting or Featured Actress in a Play – The Ritz (1975) 6. Whoopi Goldberg Ron Galella / Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images THEE Whoopi Goldberg joined the EGOT ranks in 2002, becoming the first Black performer to do so. From Sister Act and Brandy's Cinderella to Star Trek: The Next Generation and The View, Whoopi has always known how to be present in the culture. And that's not even counting her turns in Broadway stage musicals and one-woman shows! She even shows up in 30 Rock doing a bit about her EGOT status. Actually, that episode is largely responsible for the term's popularity!Emmy: Outstanding Special Class Special – Beyond Tara: The Extraordinary Life of Hattie McDaniel (2002)Grammy: Best Comedy Recording – Whoopi Goldberg: Original Broadway Show Recording (1986)Oscar: Best Actress in a Supporting Role – Ghost (1991)Tony: Best Musical – Thoroughly Modern Millie (2002) 7. Richard Rodgers Evening Standard / Getty Images Richard Rogers was better known as the "Rogers" half of Rogers and Hammerstein. The pair were responsible for musicals like Oklahoma!, Cinderella, and The Sound of Music. NBD, just the most famous musicals ever??? He also has the distinction of being the first-ever EGOT winner. Thank you for your service, sir!Emmy: Outstanding Achievement in Original Music Composed for Television – Winston Churchill: The Valiant Years (1962)Grammy: Best Show Album (Original Cast) – The Sound of Music (1961)Oscar: Best Song – "It Might as Well Be Spring" from State Fair (1946)Tony: Best Musical – South Pacific (1950) 8. Mel Brooks NBC / NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images Arguably one of the most influential people in the comedy world, Mel Brooks can do it all. He's been in the biz for over seventy years (and is still working to this day!), with smash-hit movies like Young Frankenstein, The Producers, and Spaceballs under his belt. If you're a comedian, you owe a lot to this absolute visionary actor/writer/director. Emmy: Outstanding Writing Achievement in Variety – The Sid Caesar, Imogene Coca, Carl Reiner, Howard Morris Special (1967)Grammy: Best Spoken Comedy Album – The 2000 Year Old Man in the Year 2000 (1999)Oscar: Best Story and Screenplay – Written Directly for the Screen – The Producers (1969)Tony: Best Musical – The Producers (2001) 9. Elton John Steve Granitz / WireImage The "Crocodile Rock" diva is one of our newer inductees into the EGOT Hall of Fame, joining the ranks in January 2024. Elton has been entertaining the masses for over six decades and has always found a way to win over new audiences whether it be through creating amazing music for movies like The Lion King or selling out stadiums on tour. Emmy: Outstanding Variety Special (Live) – Elton John: Farewell from Dodger Stadium (2024)Grammy: Best Male Pop Vocal Performance – "Candle in the Wind 1997" (1998)Oscar: Best Original Song – "Can You Feel the Love Tonight" (1995)Tony: Best Original Score – Aida (2000) 10. Helen Hayes Bettmann / Bettmann Archive Miss Hayes was the second person to rise to EGOT status. On top of that, she was the first woman to claim the title and we love a little herstory. Known as the "First Lady of American Theatre", Helen took her love of acting from stage to screen, nabbing the coveted award-winner status in 1977. Emmy: Best Actress – Schlitz Playhouse of Stars (1953)Grammy: Best Spoken Word Recording – Great American Documents (1977)Oscar: Best Actress in a Leading Role – The Sin of Madelon Claudet (1932)Tony: Best Actress in a Play – Happy Birthday (1947) 11. Viola Davis WWD / Penske Media via Getty Images One of the most respected actors of our time, Viola Davis knocks it out of the park in every single role she's given. You see Viola's name in the cast list? You know you're about to watch her eat it up on screen, no matter if the project is good or not. The Help may have put her on the world's radar, but Viola has been a Tony winner since 2001 and she has never stopped working hard or achieving. QUEEN!Emmy: Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series – How to Get Away with Murder (2015)Grammy: Best Audio Book, Narration & Storytelling Recording – Finding Me (2023)Oscar: Best Actress in a Supporting Role – Fences (2017)Tony: Best Featured Actress in a Play – King Hedley II (2001) 12. Andrew Lloyd Webber Theo Wargo / Getty Images for Tony Awards Productions One of the most prolific composers in the world of musical theatre, ALW is the genius man who brought the world Cats, The Phantom of the Opera, and Jesus Christ Superstar. I also have to mention Starlight Express because I can't not bring up Starlight Express. I mean, who doesn't love horny anthropomorphic trains singing on stage? I think everybody loves that.Emmy: Outstanding Variety Special (Live) – Jesus Christ Superstar Live in Concert (2018)Grammy: Best Cast Show Album – Evita: Premier American Recording (1981)Oscar: Best Original Song – "You Must Love Me" (1997)Tony: Best Musical – Cats (1983) 13. John Gielgud Hulton Archive / Getty Images Another history maker, John Gielgud was not only the first queer person to EGOT, he was also the oldest, nabbing his fourth and final award at the age of 87. Never give up on your dreams kids! The English actor/director had an illustrious theatre career on the West End before getting more into film and television and continued working until his death in 2000.Emmy: Outstanding Lead Actor in a Miniseries or a Special – Summer's Lease (1991)Grammy: Best Spoken Word, Documentary or Drama Recording – Ages of Man (1980)Oscar: Best Actor in a Supporting Role – Arthur (1982)Tony: Best Director of a Drama – Big Fish, Little Fish (1961) 14. John Legend Kevin Winter / Getty Images Multi-hyphenate John Legend lived up to his last name when he became the first Black man to EGOT in 2018. He's also one of the first people in the exclusive EGOT club who works primarily as a recording artist, though he does his fair share of producing too, and has taken home 37 major awards for his work out of an impressive 135 nominations. Come on now, John Legend!Emmy: Outstanding Variety Special (Live) – Jesus Christ Superstar Live in Concert (2018)Grammy: Best New Artist (2006)Oscar: Best Original Song – "Glory" (2015)Tony: Best Revival of a Play – Jitney (2017) 15. Marvin Hamlisch Ron Galella / Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images Get this: Marvin Hamlisch was accepted into the Juliard Pre-College program when he was SIX YEARS OLD! Ummmm, prodigy much? The composer made a name for himself writing music for A Chorus Line, Sophie's Choice, and How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days. Talk about versatility!Emmy: Outstanding Individual Achievement in Music Direction – Barbra: The Concert (1995)Grammy: Song of the Year – "The Way We Were" (1975)Oscar: Best Original Dramatic Score – The Way We Were (1974)Tony: Best Musical Score – A Chorus Line (1976) 16. Tim Rice JMEnternational / Getty Images Tim Rice is the lyricist behind pretty much all of your favorite childhood songs, working on movies like The Lion King, Aladdin, and The Road to El Dorado. He must have been thinking about becoming an EGOT member when he was writing "I Just Can't Wait to be King" because that's exactly what he is. Emmy: Outstanding Variety Special (Live) – Jesus Christ Superstar Live in Concert (2018)Grammy: Song of the Year – "A Whole New World (Aladdin's Theme)" (1994)Oscar: Best Original Song – "Can You Feel the Love Tonight" (1995)Tony: Best Book of a Musical – Evita (1980) 17. Benj Pasek and Justin Paul Nicholas Hunt / Getty Images for NARAS The team behind Lala Land and The Greatest Showman share every award they've won, so even though they are their own people, their write-up on this list would be identical. There's something nice about that though! Navigating the entertainment industry with a partner sounds pretty nice. Whatever happened to collaborating these days? I wish me and my bestie had matching EGOTs! 18. Jonathan Tunick New York Daily News Archive / NY Daily News via Getty Images Jonathan Tunick is best known for his collaborations with Broadway royalty Steven Sondheim, orchestrating and composing music for productions like Company, Into the Woods, and Sweeney Todd. Ok, bonafide icon status! These shows are synonymous with American theatre. Emmy: Outstanding Achievement in Music Direction – Night of 100 Stars (1982)Grammy: Best Instrumental Arrangement Accompanying Vocals – "No One is Alone" (1989)Oscar: Best Original Song Score and Its Adaptation or Adaptation Score – A Little Night Music (1978)Tony: Best Orchestrations – Titanic (1997) 19. Mike Nichols Carlo Allegri / Getty Images Mike Nichols was a truly legendary director known for his iconic movies like The Graduate and Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?. He was also well-respected in the comedy scene, improvising with The Compass Players comedy troupe (which would later become The Second City) where he met Elaine May. As in the famous comedy duo Nichols and May!Emmy: Outstanding Directing for a Miniseries or a Movie – Wit (2001)Grammy: Best Comedy Performance – An Evening with Mike Nichols and Elaine May (1962)Oscar: Best Director – The Graduate (1968)Tony: Best Direction of a Play – Barefoot in the Park (1964) 20. Scott Rudin NBC / NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images Scott Rudin certainly has a complicated past as a producer. Notorious for having a hot temper, he's left a bad taste in many people's mouths, with many actors threatening to leave productions he was involved with or refusing to work with him altogether. That being said, he has quite an impressive resume, working as a producer on projects like Lady Bird, Clueless, and The Book of Mormon.Emmy: Outstanding Children's Program – He Makes Me Feel Like Dancin' (1984)Grammy: Best Musical Theater Album – The Book of Mormon: Original Broadway Cast Recording (2012)Oscar: Best Picture – No Country for Old Men ( 2008)Tony: Best Musical – Passion (1994) Who are your favorite EGOT winners? Let me know in the comments!
